title: Make tests independent of real free disk by setting the minimum to 0
summary: The shared test config (test_config in tests/common/mod.rs) gets [disk] min_free_gb = 0, so CLI tests, including the nested-run test, no longer depend on the machine's free space. A new test makes the nested run see low free space (a minimum above any real free space is not simulated; the reading is injected or the guard is exercised with simulated values) and shows it still passes. The disk guard's own tests keep showing a hold and a fail-fast with simulated values. The audience is the maintainers and verifier running cargo test on small-disk sandboxes.

defaults_applied.how: cargo test, clippy and fmt must pass; the guard stays tested with simulated values.
Criteria run the nested-run test and the disk tests rather than checking that config lines exist.
The shared test config is fixed, not just the one failing test.
Behavior criteria name the cargo commands the verifier runs.
One focused change limited to the four listed files plus drain.rs only if needed.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Fixture::new writes test_config() as the fixture repo's athena.toml, and the nested scratch copy inherits it, so setting [disk] min_free_gb = 0 there reaches the nested run.
Drain tests that exercise the hold already set their own minimum explicitly; they must keep doing so after the default becomes 0 (drain.rs may need a small edit if they rely on the default 10).

Simulating low free space for the nested run is done by an injectable free-space reading in disk.rs (e.g. an env override read only when set) or equivalent; the production default of 10 GB is unchanged.
athena.toml is not changed: the minimum is set in the test config only.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test binary`: a_nested_run_works_in_a_scratch_copy_with_fake_agents passes, and a companion test simulates low free space (below 10 GB) in the nested run's environment and still passes because the test config sets min_free_gb to 0.
Run `cargo test --locked -p athena-core disk`: the disk guard's tests still show a hold (job stays queued, 'environment: low disk') and a fail-fast with simulated low free space.
crates/athena-cli/tests/common/mod.rs test_config sets [disk] min_free_gb = 0 with a comment explaining why, and the production default (10 GB in athena-data config) is unchanged.
Run `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`: all pass, and no test in the suite reads the machine's real free disk to decide its result.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry stating that tests no longer depend on real free disk space and how the minimum or free-space reading is set in tests.

out_of_scope: Changing the production default minimum of 10 GB

urgent_reason: Disk-dependent tests cause failed and rejected jobs (such as 38jx) and redo-work retries on small sandboxes, so fixing them cuts wasted time.
